reason: Trusted reviews (viewing reports, reporter bars, cases) is a multi-stage feature. Its privacy and status invariants are non-obvious and must hold across every stage, so the next session on this feature should start with them rather than rediscover them from the plan.

Stage 1 decision and warning-sign rules were stated in the spec and repeated in the Task 3 and Task 4 briefs, but the project skill only lists statuses and retention. A later session editing cases would not know who may decide what, or that a failed SIM check must not block a renter.

A Task 3 reviewer found the phone report page mapped every refusal to one message, so a signed-out renter was sent into number re-verification and a barred reporter was told they were not at the address. The refusal reasons are a contract the next session must honour in every caller.

The review found the isNull(bannedAt) guard had lost its only test while double bans became reachable. The ban-versus-uphold status overlap was recorded as a known gap, so the next session touching bans needs both facts in the domain skill.

Spec §4.8 is the rule behind the soft note. The trace shows the controller and reviewers repeatedly quoting it, but the domain skill that governs reports and cases did not state it, so a later edit could make an open case turn the badge amber or name the problem.

Stage 1 plan drops reviewDismissedAt in its final task (Task 7, with seed and dismissHold removed first). The skill still says to keep it until 'the stage the plan names', which is now stale and would make the drop look premature. Reconciling the supersession.

Stage-1 Task 6 turned the renter-side report refusals and the privacy/consent copy into rules a future editor of the phone pages or the report route could break. The skill covers only the decision and retention rules, not these user-visible invariants.

Final whole-branch review found that /review showed a generic "Try again" on 409, so a reviewer whose ban lost a race to a dismissal believed the ban had landed. The 409 body must carry the current status and the UI must branch on it.
Final review found the /privacy paragraph still described a repeated-reports threshold, which contradicts the single-upheld-case rule now in the code.

The episode decided a landlord is only verified or banned: amber, Confirm warning and published problem counts are removed, and a ban stores case status `banned`. The existing trusted-reviews skill still documents uphold, 🟠 and `upheld` as live rules, so it would keep steering future sessions into the superseded design. Rewriting it in place reconciles the library.
The decision set is in the skill but the user-facing button labels are not. A future edit could rename or drop one, so the labels belong next to the decision rule.
The ban-status rename (`upheld` to `banned`) means rehearsal databases with old rows show stale results until reseeded. The skill states the rule but not the reseed step.

The /privacy paragraph said only a ban changes a listing, which was untrue because an open report adds the under-review note. The required replacement copy is now pinned so the next edit does not reintroduce the claim.
